chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said, “O Messenger of Allah, my wife does not repel the hand of one who touches.” He said, “Then divorce her.” The man said, “O Messenger of Allah, I love her.” He said, “Then keep her.”

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, to whom the man brought his question
key_terms.امْرَأَتِي: my wife; the spouse about whom the complaint was made
key_terms.فَأَمْسِكْهَا: then keep her; the subsequent instruction after the man stated his attachment
key_terms.فَطَلِّقْهَا: then divorce her; the initial directive given
key_terms.لَا تَدْفَعُ: does not repel or ward off; indicating lack of resistance
key_terms.يَدَ لَامِسٍ: the hand of one who touches; referring to physical contact

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say about a man whose wife did not repel the touch of other men?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a man’s complaint to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about his wife’s improper conduct with men and records the Prophet’s response. It presents a legal and familial scenario involving marriage, moral concern, and the option of divorce or remaining with one’s spouse.
